messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate observed in eu-west-1 inference gateway. Severity: P2. Paging on-call (mike_oncall). Key signal: 5xx spike + 200ms tail latency increase for small-chat routes.

mike_oncall: on it. can someone grab quick blast radius? first check: is this routing or model-side?

sarah_sre: looking at gateway logs — upstream shows burst of connection resets to the runtime pool for low-priority lanes. CPU/GPU hosts look healthy but queue length on the transformer workers jumped.

julia_prodops: customer-impact: alerting shows ~4.8% of requests returning 503 over last 6m, mostly free-tier and low-tier customers in EU region, a few dev accounts. No dedicated customers flagged yet.

mike_oncall: ok plan: 1) emergency rate-limit free-tier in eu-west to 8 req/s per org, 2) steer low-tier traffic from eu-west to us-east with weight 30%, 3) disable streaming for non-enterprise chats in eu-west to reduce connection churn. Will execute in that order.

kevin_infra: prepping routing change. I’ll push a temporary policy:
```
redwoodctl routing update --region eu-west-1 --policy emergency-steer-1865432100 \
  --rules '[{"match":"tier==low","steer_to":"us-east-1","weight":0.3}]'
```
Applying now.

incident-bot: ACTION: routing policy emergency-steer-1865432100 applied by kevin_infra.

mike_oncall: applying rate-limit to free-tier now:
```
redwoodctl ratelimit create --scope=org_tier:free --region=eu-west-1 --qps=8 --burst=16 --note="emergency - steer"
```

incident-bot: ACTION: rate-limit created (id rl-6291).

sarah_sre: disabling streaming for non-enterprise chat in eu-west: flipping feature flag ff_disable_streaming_lowtier in feature-store.

julia_prodops: notifying support and status page: small number of EU dev customers affected, we’ve applied mitigations (rate-limits + steering). ETA: 20m to stabilize, will update.

eva_support: posting initial advisory to #customer-notifications: "We’re seeing degraded responses for free accounts in EU. Mitigations in place. Monitoring. Please DM if you see user-facing errors."

mike_oncall: monitoring metrics — 2 min after changes: 5xx rate dropped from 4.8% -> 2.1%, queue length down ~45%, p95 latency on small-chat back to baseline-ish. Good signal.

sarah_sre: side note — telemetry shows a specific runtime build (rtd-2026-07-05-eu) has higher KV cache miss under this workload on longer sessions; we should patch as follow-up but not during current live mitigation.

kevin_infra: routing rollbacks ready if we overshoot. I nudged weight to 0.3 only; can increase to 0.5 if needed.

mike_oncall: quick customer-impact check: enterprise orgs unaffected, no SLA breach. Marking customer-impact as low/medium. Julia, can you coordinate a short post-incident update for the status page in 1h?

julia_prodops: yep — will draft.

incident-bot: NOTE: on-call handoff scheduled in 45m. mike_oncall please confirm if you want to hand to sarah_sre or stay.

mike_oncall: I’ll stay for the first hour to ensure stability, then hand to sarah_sre for deep investigation. Assigning postmortem owner to julia_prodops.

sarah_sre: will take over after mike if anything regresses. immediate next steps for postmortem: gather routing traces, kernel selection metrics for rtd-2026-07-05-eu, and per-org request breakdown.

kevin_infra: additional mitigation option if traffic surges again: temporarily pin enterprise traffic to dedicated lanes only and reject low-priority at edge with 429+Retry-After to protect capacity. Don’t prefer, but ready.

mike_oncall: noted. For now, maintain rate-limit + steer + streaming-disable. Monitoring for 30m. If 5xx goes <1% and queue lengths stable, we’ll start relaxing.

(12m later)

mike_oncall: update: metrics stable. 5xx ~0.9%, latency p95 normalized. Removing streaming-disable for low-tier now as load reduced to avoid UX regression.

sarah_sre: re-enabling streaming flag.

incident-bot: ACTION: ff_disable_streaming_lowtier rolled back by sarah_sre.

mike_oncall: leaving rate-limit and steering in place for additional 30m as guardrail. If stable, we’ll remove steering weight (set back to 0) and then remove rate-limit.

julia_prodops: drafted status page update and sent to #comm-ops for quick review. ETA 5m.

eva_support: queued customer messages for impacted dev orgs explaining cause and actions.

mike_oncall: final note for handoff: postmortem owner julia_prodops; primary investigators: sarah_sre, kevin_infra; follow-ups: runtime patch for cache behavior (eng-ml), improved routing playbook to detect cache-driven spikes (eng-runtime), and an emergency runbook tweak to prefer 429s over 503s for graceful throttling.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied and partially rolled back. Current severity: P3 (monitoring). Next update scheduled in 30m or on handoff.

mike_oncall: handing over to sarah_sre for continued watch. leaving note: keep steering weight at 0.3 if any queue jitter > 20% and be ready to cut to 0.5.

sarah_sre: acknowledged. taking over.

(Handed off)

julia_prodops: postmortem placeholder created and assigned. Will collate logs and timeline, aim to publish within 72h. Action items created in JIRA: RD-3421 (runtime cache investigation), OPS-1287 (routing playbook update), COMM-99 (customer comms followup).

mike_oncall: thx team. closing page.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: mitigations successful, monitoring ongoing.
